paragraphs.text: Microsoft ILT course content master template
PowerPoint presentation template for ILT courses
Delete these slides before distribution. They are intended only for guidance.
How to use the ILT course PowerPoint templateFollow these tips to help transition slides to this template from previous designs.

When inserting content into the new template from another deck, copy the slide(s) and choose “Use Destination Theme” when pasting. This is the safest way to ensure you’re not creating extra masters (and bloating the file size).

After pasting, you may need to adjust the formatting to fit the new template's layout. Pay attention to font sizes, line spacing, alignment, and any other formatting elements that may need fine-tuning.
Apply a master to your slides

To apply a master layout to a slide, click Home > Layout and choose from the available options. If the copied content doesn't fit correctly into the new placeholders, you may need to copy and paste the content into the corresponding placeholders manually.
To restore a slide’s placeholders, go to Home > Slides > Reset. Reset only restores placeholders defined by the layout. Custom text boxes, shapes, and pictures you added aren’t restored or removed.
Use icons sparingly as visual cues or to break up large amounts of text. A full glyph library is included in the appendix, organized by theme.
A simple set of monoline icons is available at the end of this deck, with links to the full Monoline icon set on Brand Central.
For additional resources, refer to the last page of this deck.

This should be strategy for taking the exam, not teaching the concepts. Assume viewers already have working knowledge and experience.
Use the phrasing patterns in the band below to emphasize what to watch for.
Don’t mistake the difference between X and Y…
This would be a great exercise to practice in a lab…
This is one of the most important concepts for the exam…
This is similar to X, but here’s what is different…
This just changed recently, so make sure you understand…
Remember this can be done in X number of ways…
One thing you need to remember here is…
Here’s an example of how we use this feature at Microsoft…
The main thing I want to call out here is…
Replace non-inclusive verbs in your delivery. A find-and-replace pass on your script will catch most of them.
Use: observe, go to, refer to, show, notice, note, select, enter.
Avoid: see, as you see here, look, view, click, right-click, walk through, type, hit.
For series intros and outros, use the intro-outro script provided.
For the remaining slides, use the guiding points to prepare your own script.
Keep within the duration shown on each slide. Slide durations roll up to the functional group (FG) total.
Highlight parts of a slide with arrows or boxes during delivery.

Note to MTT: This deck is split into sections based on the functional groups of this exam. The first functional groups include introduction slides which have a specific script which we recommend you follow. 
Similarly, the first slide of each section also has a specific script. This has been provided to you in a separate intro-outro script.
For other slides, you will have to create your own script based on the “guidelines for script” added in the notes section.

paragraphs.text: Take the following steps to create content that everyone can consume effectively.
Use high contrast colors for maximum readability. The recommended contrast is 4.5:1.
Download the Color Contrast Analyzer to determine the legibility of text and the contrast of visual elements
Use different shapes with a legend to indicate statuses to accommodate for color blindness.Example:
Alt text helps people with screen readers understand the content of slides. You should create alternate text for shapes, pictures, charts, tables, SmartArt graphics, or other objects.Here’s how:
If an object is meant to add visual styling and doesn’t contain meaning, do not add alt text and instead check Mark as decorative

Using built-in slide layout that matches your content ensures a hierarchical reading order of text blocks. Example: If a new slide will have a title, rather than starting with a blank layout and adding a text block for the title, choose one of the built-in layouts with a title placeholder.

Screen readers describe content on the screen in the order it was created. To ensure your content is read back in the order you prefer, arrange your objects in the Selection Pane appropriately. Objects on the bottom of the selection pane are read first. Here’s how:
In the Drawing group, select the Arrange drop-down menu
Be sure to run the Accessibility Checker:
Click the Check for Issues drop down menu

Videos need to be accessible: if your presentation includes a video, ensure it is captioned and audio described (if appropriate)Visit the Office Accessibility Center to learn more about accessibility in PowerPoint.
